api: POST https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/search/works (JSON SearchParameters body {q, limit, offset}; documented twin: GET https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/search/works/?q=<q>&limit=<n>&offset=<n>) with header Authorization: Bearer <CORE_API_KEY> — the key is read from the CORE_API_KEY environment variable (repo Actions secret); full text: the hit's own downloadUrl / sourceFulltextUrls entry, or the Discovery operation POST https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/discover (DiscoveryParameters {doi, title, year} -> DiscoveryResponse {fullTextLink, source}) resolving a free full-text link for a DOI-only hit; spec's own file route: GET https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/works/{identifier}/download
name: CORE — Connecting Repositories (core.ac.uk), The Open University
notes: LIVE-WIRED §42 (docs-verified 2026-11-26): CORE, the Open University's global aggregator of open-access research papers (300M+ metadata records, tens of millions of harvested full texts from 10,000+ repositories and journals). API shape verified against the OFFICIAL OpenAPI specification (https://api.core.ac.uk/swagger/v3.json, the document behind the Swagger UI at https://api.core.ac.uk/docs/v3): (1) SEARCH — POST /v3/search/{entityType} with a JSON SearchParameters body {q, limit, offset} (GET /v3/search/{entityType}/ is the documented twin) answers a SearchResponse {totalHits, limit, offset, results: [Work]}; a Work carries downloadUrl ('The URL from where you can download the full text of the work'), fullText ('plain text extraction of the full text document') and sourceFulltextUrls ('A list of all the URLs where this document can be downloaded from'); the spec prints snake_case names, the live API answers camelCase — the parser accepts both. (2) DISCOVERY — the operation Jupiter pointed at (docs tag 'Discovery', operation post_discovery): POST /v3/discover with a DiscoveryParameters body {doi, title, year, eprints_id, plugin_id, referrer} answers a DiscoveryResponse {fullTextLink, source}; the tag and both schemas are verified in the OpenAPI document, the path string is the one recorded by the official documentation's write-ups of the Discovery API; used ONLY to resolve a full-text link for a search hit that carries a DOI but no download URL, fail-soft under a small per-call budget. (3) AUTH — the spec's security schemes offer the key as an api_key query parameter or as the header 'Authorization: Bearer [API_KEY]'; the header is used. (4) FULL-TEXT DISCIPLINE — a hit is emitted ONLY when it carries a downloadUrl or a sourceFulltextUrls entry (or Discovery resolves one for its DOI); candidates carry oa_pdf_url and flow into attach_fulltexts_v2's index-fulltext route, exactly like §34/§36; metadata-only hits are skipped per the full-text-only law; the query is first biased with the documented _exists_:fullText clause (CORE API v3 announcement), with one plain-query retry if it returns nothing. History: CORE was already in the pool three times — sources_registry_2 (plain index entry, api https://api.core.ac.uk/v3), thesis_registry (thesis archive) and world_libraries_registry §27, where it stayed REGISTRY-ONLY under the no-key law after the unkeyed probe answered HTTP 429 (the unkeyed API also withholds fullText from public users). The §40 survey classed CORE A (wireable after a free email-only registration); Jupiter registered himself on 2026-11-26 and the key was emailed to him. This entry's URL (https://core.ac.uk) therefore duplicates the older records in the pool: loaded count rises by one, the unique-URL count is unchanged (first record wins for §17 matching — the wiring itself lives in search_core, not in this record). KEY STATE / HONEST CAVEAT: the engine reads CORE_API_KEY from the environment and is DORMANT (fail-soft, no request made) until Jupiter pastes the key ONCE into the repo's Actions secrets; no keyed live smoke has run yet — this wiring rests on the official spec + the mocked-shape tests in test_core.py, and the keyed smoke is owed the moment the secret lands.
